name: Curve pETH/ETH Vyper lock reentrancy
summary: Vyper 0.2.15 allocated the same named nonreentrant lock to different storage slots in different functions. The pETH/ETH pool's native-ETH callback therefore allowed cross-function reentrancy from remove_liquidity() into add_liquidity(), minting an invalid claim on pool reserves.

loss.notes: The exploit receipt records exactly 86,106.654659206663837483 WETH wrapped after the pool operations, 80,000 WETH repaid to Balancer, and 6,106.654659206663837483 WETH transferred as net proceeds. Later recovery is separate from exploit-time loss. Other Vyper-affected pools were attacked independently and are not included.

ageReset.description: Curve's factory deployed an immutable 45-byte EIP-1167 clone whose runtime embeds implementation 0x6326debbaa15bcfe603d831e7d75f4fc10d9b43e. Both clone and implementation runtimes remained unchanged through the exploit.

sources.note: Reviewed the exploit receipt and call trace, pool creation transaction and trace, the clone and implementation runtimes at historical boundaries, verified Vyper 0.2.15 source, commit-pinned reproduction, Vyper's compiler advisory, LlamaRisk's pool-by-pool post-mortem, and exact WETH flows. The exploit calls pETH/ETH pool 0x9848482da3ee3076165ce6497eda906e66bb85c5 and every affected pool frame delegates to 0x6326debbaa15bcfe603d831e7d75f4fc10d9b43e. The pool's 45-byte EIP-1167 runtime embeds that address and hashes to 0xbed04db3507e08e5220f6eadf98d5df05bdbc74df129c73fcbab7c441e86b124. Factory 0xb9fc157394af804a3578134a6585c0dc9cc990d4 created the clone in transaction 0x659f0eb12c4edf042be41885ed1a8bc78b0a2e87ca47339031b9253cd7ae61ce; the transaction sender was 0x7a271674b5fae043f42f183092f48fb06d6d551b. The 17,535-byte implementation existed before clone activation and retained hash 0xba0284a6a8a86734c1c777e3c6b5b56f2c8ba95dc0f7eba481c6d09da7885ebc through block 17806055. The exploit wraps 86,106.654659206663837483 WETH, repays the 80,000 WETH flash loan, and transfers the exact remainder as proceeds.
Clone basis retained under the case-by-case rule: the pETH/ETH clone supplied the pool configuration and accumulated liquidity that made the shared compiler defect exploitable for this loss.
